sentences.text: (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
The captioned appeal is by the claimants who have questioned the compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.698/2015.
The respondent No.2/Insurance company admits its liability.
The appeal is purely on quantum.
2. The appellants herein who are father and sister have filed a claim petition for having lost one Ambrish in a road traffic accident dated 19.10.2015.
The claimants and the Insurance company let in oral and documentary evidence.

The Tribunal in absence of income proof, assessed the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.8,000/- and without adding future prospects has awarded a sum of Rs.8,64,000/- towards loss of dependency.
In all, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.8,94,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance company.

4. The claimants though contended that deceased was aged 20 years and was into supply of milk and newspaper and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, no documentary evidence is placed on record to substantiate his income.
In absence of income proof, this Court is of the view that Tribunal was justified in notionally assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/-.
However, Tribunal erred in not adding future prospects.
Having regard to the fact that deceased was hardly aged 20 years

,
40% needs to be added towards future prospects.
Accordingly, the income is assessed at Rs.11,200/-.

After deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses, the income is notionally assessed at Rs.7,466.67/- and by applying multiplier of 18, the compensation payable under head 'loss of dependency' works out to Rs.16,12,799/- rounded off to Rs.16,12,800/- (7,466.67x12x18).
Under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.1,10,000/- is awarded.

The accident is of the year 2015 and therefore, 10% escalation for every three years in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1, which works out to Rs.22,000/- is added.

sentences.text: The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.17,44,800/- as against Rs.8,94,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
